community: Remote & backcountry, Peace River Regional District

description.value: A remote backcountry wilderness set on Kakwa Lake beneath 3000m peaks and sweeping alpine meadows on the Continental Divide; mountain bikes can ride the final Tote Road section but the first 75km from the staging site requires a 4x4 high-clearance vehicle, and no potable water is available at the park.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms Kakwa Lake is a backcountry tent-camping area within Kakwa Park, accessible by mountain bike and Class 1 e-bikes only on the final Tote Road segment (Class 2 and 3 e-bikes are explicitly restricted beyond the park boundary). The website provides explicit negative evidence that potable water is unavailable ('Bring your own drinking water. Potable water is not available at the park.') and confirms a first-come, first-served public cabin exists at the lake. No formal campsite amenities (showers, laundry, charging, tools, etc.) are mentioned, consistent with the extreme remoteness (~100km from staging on rough 4x4 forest service road).
concerns: OSM node is named 'Kakwa Lake' (a geographic feature) rather than a formal named campsite; the camping use is confirmed by BC Parks but there is no distinct campsite name.
No address available; location is extremely remote backcountry with no civic address.
Class 2 and Class 3 e-bikes are explicitly prohibited on the Tote Road (park boundary to Kakwa Lake); only Class 1 e-bikes permitted on that final segment.
Access road (Walker Creek FSR) described as 'uneven, rutted, slippery and very rough' and recommended for 4x4 high-clearance vehicles only — unusual barrier for touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Kakwa Lake is genuinely accessible by mountain bike and Class 1 e-bike, making it relevant to adventure cyclists, but it is an extremely remote backcountry site (~100 km on rough 4x4 forest service road from the staging area) with no amenities beyond a first-come, first-served cabin — reviewers should confirm whether this level of expedition-grade remoteness fits the WWC directory's intended audience.
enrichment_extras.notes: The park forms part of the Kakwa Willmore Interprovincial Park, shared with Alberta's Kakwa Wildlands Park and Willmore Wilderness Park. Wildlife viewing and wilderness photography are highlighted draws. Snowmobile access is seasonal (December 1 to April 15 or 30).
